title: Divide a String Into Groups of Size k
summary: Given a string s, a group size k, and a fill character, divide s into groups where each group contains k characters.
statement: Given a string s, a group size k, and a fill character, divide s into groups where each group contains k characters. If the last group is not of size k, append the fill character until it reaches size k. Return an array of strings, where each string represents one of the groups, such that removing the fill character from the last group (if it exists) and concatenating all the groups in order results in the original string s.
constraints: s is nonempty, k is positive, and fill is one character.
Split s consecutively into groups of exactly k characters.
Pad only the final short group with fill until its length is k.
reference_solution:
def divide_filled_groups(s,k,fill):
    return [s[index:index+k].ljust(k,fill) for index in range(0,len(s),k)]
hints: Fixed-step slicing naturally preserves order and isolates only the possibly short final chunk.
Take s[index:index+k] for indices 0,k,2k,... and right-pad each slice to k.
All nonfinal slices already have size k; only the last receives exactly the missing number of fill characters.
editorial: All nonfinal slices already have size k; only the last receives exactly the missing number of fill characters.

tests.explanation: The string divides evenly into abc, def, and ghi with no padding.
The final j is padded twice, producing jxx.
